races.name: Heineken Low & No Bar Ebf Maiden Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Bacha
runners_data.note: Ran 3rd and 5th on good ground at Goodwood and Sandown respectively, giving it fair form for this grade — a natural hold-up type who will be ridden from the rear despite appearing on the midfield map due to overcrowding of closers; soft ground is not a concern on breeding but the slow early pace may make ground-making harder.|

runners_data.name: Perryston
runners_data.note: Finished a well-beaten 10th on good at Goodwood last time and carries a ⚠ fade flag — Kevin Stott takes the mount but the form is thin and the horse's tendency to not see out the finish is a material negative on soft ground where the final climb bites.|

runners_data.name: Stay On Tab
runners_data.note: Has run five times without winning, placing 3rd once, and has zero wins or places on similar soft going (0W0P in 1 comparable run) — a hold-up type that has been mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear, and with a headgear flag and a 3-claim apprentice aboard, this looks a difficult position to win from.|

runners_data.name: Classyfied
runners_data.note: Placed 4th and 5th on good at Goodwood, showing consistent mid-division form for Tim Easterby — a hold-up runner who will be positioned around midfield and whose chance hinges on the pace being quick enough to bring closers into play on soft ground.|

runners_data.name: Dadawada
runners_data.note: Holds soft-ground form (4th on soft last time) and is trained by Christopher Kellett who has had no winners in the last 14 days; a genuine prominent type who should sit just off the leader and represents one of the more plausible threats to Sod Hall Lane if the pace-setter tires.|

runners_data.name: Royal Strike
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's yard has had 9 winners in 14 days which is the strongest recent trainer form in the race — Royal Strike ran 3rd and 4th over 6f on good/standard ground, stepping down to 5f on soft is worth monitoring, but Clifford Lee is a capable rider and the prominent style suits this pace shape.|

runners_data.name: Sneakin Pete
runners_data.note: No form available, making going suitability and trip unknown — lightly raced flag and debut status means this runner is a complete wildcard, though an unknown juvenile can always spring a surprise in a weak maiden field.|

runners_data.name: Sod Hall Lane
runners_data.note: Finished 2nd on debut over 5f on good at Carlisle, showing enough pace to take the lead naturally — Declan Carroll's yard has had just 1 winner in 14 days but the horse's front-running role is confirmed, and with no rival likely to take it on for the lead on soft ground, the tactical position is highly favourable; STYLE_FIT note applies as a LEAD horse mapped to prominent, but that is a minor concern since it is still the race-shaper.|

races.paceDynamic: Sod Hall Lane is the confirmed lone front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop from the front on soft ground at Hamilton. Dadawada and Royal Strike are the two prominent types and will slot in behind, but neither looks likely to apply serious pressure to Sod Hall Lane, meaning the pace is likely to be honest rather than brutal. The field nominally contains more hold-up horses (Bacha, Stay On Tab, Classyfied, Perryston) than the track shape can accommodate at the rear — Bacha and Stay On Tab are genuine closers pushed into midfield on the map because the rear is over-subscribed, but in practice the slower early tempo on soft ground may compress the field anyway. A steady, front-runner-controlled 5f on soft turf at Hamilton favours horses that can travel prominently or at least in the slipstream of the leader, as soft ground blunts late acceleration and the uphill finish rewards those who conserve energy while on the bridle, not those forced to make ground from off a slow pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sod Hall Lane Controls Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Sod Hall Lane leads unchallenged and sets a measured soft-ground tempo that drains late closers.
scenarios.body: Sod Hall Lane dictates from the front with Dadawada and Royal Strike covering the gaps, and the soft ground means hold-up runners face too much ground to make up in the final furlong; prominent types who tracked the leader on the bridle arrive with the most energy at the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Strike or Dadawada track the leader closely and Sod Hall Lane fades in the final 100 yards after setting the pace.
scenarios.body: A pace-led race where the front-runner ties up allows a well-placed prominent tracker to pounce at the Hamilton hill; Royal Strike has experience at 6f and Dadawada has soft-ground form, both relevant to this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely quick enough to set up a true soft-ground test that rewards a strong finish.
scenarios.body: Classyfied or Bacha, travelling in midfield off the tempo, find the front-runners stopping in front of them up the rise and pick them off late; this scenario is partially discounted because Bacha is redistributed from its natural hold-up role and may not achieve ideal position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutant Shock
scenarios.trigger: If Sneakin Pete breaks smartly, shows natural ability on debut and benefits from an inexperienced field under soft conditions.
scenarios.body: An unknown quantity on debut can upset a weak maiden if it settles kindly and shows raw class; the trainer has limited recent runners and going is unproven, but soft-ground debut winners at 5f are not uncommon in this grade.

watchPoints.text: Sod Hall Lane's early stride pattern — if it jumps cleanly and immediately clears, the race is effectively over for hold-up types within the first furlong on soft ground.
Royal Strike's response to the step down from 6f to 5f on soft — Burke's horse has only raced over 6f and may be caught for toe early before finding its stride too late.

Bacha and Stay On Tab — both are genuine hold-up types pushed into a midfield map position; watch whether they can actually achieve even that berth or whether soft ground and a slow pace leaves them with too much to do.

Dadawada's headgear — the horse runs with headgear noted and has soft-ground form; monitor whether it travels smoothly behind Sod Hall Lane in the early stages as that is the key indicator of its chance.
Sneakin Pete on debut — any sign of natural early speed from the stalls would rapidly upgrade its chance in a field where only one confirmed pace-setter exists.

races.name: Hampton By Hilton Hotel Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Edgewater Drive
runners_data.note: Prominent-running 5yo with wins on soft and a live chance fresh off 298 days — the layoff is a major flag, but Wilf Storey has just one run in the last 14 days and soft going suits based on a 10/15 similar-going record with four wins; drop back from 7f shapes this as a speed-on trip fit.

runners_data.name: Lumenbourg
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's 5yo has won on soft and arrives on a 41-day break in good form — the recent 4th, 6th and 4th sequence masks a soft-ground win and three placed efforts at this trip, making him one of the more consistent prominent types in the field.

runners_data.name: Iris Dancer
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner — soft-ground OK, has won on good and placed on soft at this trip, and Tristan Davidson's yard is 4/10 in the last 14 days; uncontested lead on a soft Hamilton 6f is a significant tactical advantage for this 8yo veteran.

runners_data.name: Camera Shy
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator for Michael Dods who arrives 27 days fresh — all recent starts have come at 6f-7f on standard or good ground, so the soft test is untried, but Connor Beasley's experience is a positive and the horse's ability to sit off a slow pace without overcrowding is an advantage here.

runners_data.name: Big Apple Jack
runners_data.note: This 4yo ran 2nd in soft on his best recent effort — he is a true rear-of-field type who will find himself shuffled into midfield given the number of hold-up runners in this field, and that compromised position tempers his chance considerably even if the soft going theoretically suits.

runners_data.name: White Umbrella
runners_data.note: Won on soft at Southwell and has the headgear angle, but this 7yo naturally settles last and will be unable to access that position in a field this crowded at the rear — Paul Mulrennan will have to commit forward earlier than ideal, which alters the entire race model for him.

runners_data.name: Mount Ruapehu
runners_data.note: Six-year-old prominent type for Iain Jardine who has been quietly consistent without winning — zero wins in 15 similar-going runs is a significant concern on soft, and recent 6th, 8th, 4th, 6th, 6th form offers limited confidence even if the pace shape suits his style.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 6yo won at 6f on good ground but has placed on soft — the visor headgear is noted, and while the yard is in form (3/29), this is a genuine hold-up horse who will struggle to get his natural trailing position with so many rivals occupying that space; his best chance rests on a dramatic pace collapse.

runners_data.name: Summerstorms Dream
runners_data.note: A 4yo who has shown form placing on good ground at 5f-6f but carries no wins from 13 similar-going starts — Lauren Young takes the 5lb claim, but this is a true come-from-behind type who will be denied her natural berth and faces the steepest challenge of the redistributed group.

runners_data.name: Valentine Catcher
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 5yo is a consistent hold-up performer — 4/15 similar-going record with a 2nd and no wins suggests soft is manageable rather than ideal, and David Allan rides, but finishing 9th and 7th in recent starts at 7f-8f makes 6f a more likely fit; traffic risk is real in this field configuration.

runners_data.name: Lesley's Boy
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr picks up the ride for the Faheys on this 4yo who ran 16th on soft last time — the visor is worn and soft going has a poor record (16th being the standout negative), and while Orr is an upgrade in the saddle, the hold-up style and soft form make this a difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Men Of Honour
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 4yo has six runs in similar going and has been competitive without winning — the recent 5th, 9th, 6th, 9th, 9th sequence is discouraging, and with no headgear, no wins and an 11-day turnaround, this hold-up horse faces the same traffic problems as the rest of the rear-end brigade.

runners_data.name: Impressor
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with 10 similar-going runs and a win on soft — Phillip Makin's charge is a hold-up type at heart and will be unable to get to the back of this field, meaning Sam James will find him racing out of his natural rhythm; the soft form is the best angle but the positional compromise is significant.

races.paceDynamic: Iris Dancer is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will stride into a comfortable, uncontested position from the gates and control tempo on soft ground at Hamilton's 6f. The soft going will naturally compress the pace, meaning Iris Dancer can dictate a rhythm that plays to her strengths without burning energy repelling a pressing rival — this is a sustainable lead scenario, not a contested one. With the majority of this 13-runner field composed of hold-up horses who will be forced into midfield or just off the pace due to overcrowding at the rear, the race shape is dominated by horses attempting to come from a position they cannot naturally achieve. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers and horses with the ability to travel close to a modest, uncontested pace on soft ground are most favoured; the overcrowded hold-up section means true closers will be bottled in and may find traffic with no clean route through. Several runners tagged as redistributed — including Impressor, Big Apple Jack, White Umbrella, Doon The Glen and Summerstorms Dream — are genuine hold-up types who cannot all secure their preferred rear position and will be shuffled into midfield, making them unreliable beneficiaries of any late-run scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Iris Dancer Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Iris Dancer leads from the front unopposed and the soft ground slows the race to a tempo that rewards her natural front-running style.
scenarios.body: Iris Dancer sets a controlled, energy-conserving pace with no rival willing or able to press her, and the modest gallop leaves hold-up horses with insufficient ground to make up in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pressurise Late
scenarios.trigger: If Lumenbourg or Edgewater Drive track Iris Dancer tightly and sustain a challenge in the final two furlongs as soft ground kicks in.
scenarios.body: The soft surface extends the stamina test and riders travelling prominently are already in the best position to pounce when Iris Dancer ties up, with no hold-up horse able to get past the wall of midfield traffic.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Defies Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely collapses in the final furlong and a well-placed hold-up runner finds a gap through a tiring field.
scenarios.body: Camera Shy or Valentine Catcher, who are genuine hold-up types not redistributed from another role, are best placed to benefit if soft-ground attrition brings the front horses back sharply in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the soft going proves more testing than anticipated and the front end folds dramatically, opening the race up to any survivor.
scenarios.body: In a race where multiple horses are out of position and front-runners have expended energy controlling a congested field, a midfield runner with soft-ground form scrambles home in a strung-out finish.

watchPoints.text: Iris Dancer — if she breaks cleanly and crosses to the rail early, she controls this race from the front without a challenger and every subsequent scenario becomes far less likely; watch the first two furlongs closely.

Crowded hold-up section — with Impressor, Big Apple Jack, White Umbrella, Doon The Glen and Summerstorms Dream all trying to settle at the rear, watch for jostling and shuffling in the early stages that could cause interference or leave horses with nowhere to go turning for home.

Edgewater Drive — 298 days off the track is a major fitness flag; watch the paddock for signs of fitness and the early gallop to see if Greg Fairley pushes forward confidently or drops away under pressure.

Soft-ground verification — the going is confirmed soft for the 5:20 and for later 6f races, but watch for any market drifts among runners with soft concerns (Lesley's Boy in particular given the 16th on soft last time) as a signal the market has repriced that form.

Mount Ruapehu's pace position — if Jack Nicholls on the 3lb claimer pushes forward aggressively to track Iris Dancer, this could introduce minor pressure that disrupts the uncontested lead scenario and fractionally improves the hold-up horses' chances in the straight.

races.name: Every Race Live On Racing Tv Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Perseus Way
runners_data.note: Won twice on good-to-soft and soft, handles this going well, but is a genuine hold-up horse who will need the pace to be more than pedestrian over 1m5f; 73 days off is worth monitoring though trainer Davidson has hit form recently.

runners_data.name: Simply Ruby
runners_data.note: Scored on soft over 12f and has place form on similar going — a confirmed hold-up type who will sit towards the rear; the step up to 1m5f is a question mark but the going suits.

runners_data.name: Ouro Preto
runners_data.note: Consistent money in heavy-market handicaps but has been posting finishing positions in the 7-11 range on good recently; a genuine closer whose natural rear-of-field position may be compromised by the crowded hold-up division — style fit is diluted.

runners_data.name: Spanish Hustle
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran with modest recent form, all finishes between 5th and 12th; a hold-up horse at heart who will be racing against type if forced forward into midfield, and soft ground does not appear to sharpen connections' expectations given three-week return.

runners_data.name: Clocker
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race — Oisin Orr can control every fraction from flag to finish; won over 12f on good two starts ago and the step to 13f here on soft is the one question, but an uncontested lead compensates considerably.

runners_data.name: Ibn Altheeb
runners_data.note: Wore a hood last time and has placed twice from soft-ground runs, but his recent form reads 0-3-4-0 and the headgear bears watching; a hold-up horse who may find progress difficult if the pace is steady and the gaps don't materialise.

runners_data.name: Billy No Mates
runners_data.note: Decade-old stayer with soft-ground place form and a solid record at 14-16f trips; 75 days off and pushed into a midfield role out of his natural rear position, which tempers expectations despite the trip and going suiting in theory.

runners_data.name: Kindly Queen
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing a hood and one of the better-placed horses for this scenario — tracked leaders twice recently for a place; 3-year-old stepping up sharply in trip but style suits the uncontested pace shape, and her jockey Bughanaim will be alive to that.

runners_data.name: Path To Peace
runners_data.note: Tagged as fading in the finish, which is a serious flag on soft ground over 1m5f; a hold-up horse with poor recent form (9-0-6-0) and only one run on soft, making this a difficult race to get involved in.

runners_data.name: Wootton's Gal
runners_data.note: Placed over 11f on good, improving young filly from the Fahey yard; a natural hold-up type who may find herself racing in midfield against her grain in this crowded field — her best form has come on faster ground and the soft is untested.

runners_data.name: Ebony Maw
runners_data.note: Placed on soft over 15f and has soft-ground experience across multiple runs — a genuine prominent-style horse who could benefit from a position just off Clocker's back; wore a tongue-tie and blinkers, and Kevin Stott can capitalise if settled prominently.

runners_data.name: Aighear
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse with two wins on soft and a strong record at 15-16f trips, but style places her in a crowded midfield division against her preference; trainer Goldie in form but 48 days off and the redistribution challenge is real.

races.paceDynamic: Clocker is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field over 1m5f on soft ground at Hamilton, and with no genuine rival likely to dispute the lead, Oisin Orr can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front. On soft going over this extended trip, that uncontested lead is a significant tactical asset — Clocker can set whatever fractions suit, conserving enough to remain competitive deep into the straight. The redistribution note is important here: Ouro Preto, Wootton's Gal, Spanish Hustle, Billy No Mates, and Aighear are all natural hold-up horses who cannot all find their preferred rear position in a 12-runner field, meaning several will be shuffled forward into midfield against their grain, diluting the effectiveness of any late closing wave. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those capable of tracking a steady leader before unleashing a sustained — rather than sharp — finish, with genuine hold-up horses facing the dual difficulty of soft ground and a pace unlikely to be truly searching enough to guarantee the gaps they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Clocker Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Clocker dictates an uncontested, moderate pace and the field strings out on soft ground, leaving hold-up horses with too much to do.
scenarios.body: Clocker sets every fraction from the front, and with soft going dulling any finishing burst from the rear, horses tracking from a prominent position have the best chance to pick him off late or he simply holds on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or midfield tracker travels smoothly behind Clocker and pounces in the final two furlongs as the pace eases.
scenarios.body: Kindly Queen or Ebony Maw, both genuine prominent types, are ideally positioned to exploit a modest gallop by looming up turning for home and sustaining their effort on the soft surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the field comes back to the hold-up horses, allowing one genuine closer to reel them in.
scenarios.body: Perseus Way has the best soft-ground hold-up profile in the field and the form to suggest a late run is possible if the gallop is honest enough; Simply Ruby also has a win on soft and could finish off.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Collapse In Soft Ground
scenarios.trigger: If the soft going proves particularly testing and several prominent horses tire badly, leaving one proven stayer with soft-ground resilience to grind past the field late.
scenarios.body: A genuinely gruelling test could elevate the stayers with proven soft form, but most redistribution horses racing out of role are most exposed here, making this the least reliable scenario.

watchPoints.text: Clocker — watch how Oisin Orr handles the early stages; if he is allowed to dictate a completely uncontested soft gallop, this horse's chances are materially enhanced and the entire pace map shifts around him.

Kindly Queen and Ebony Maw — both genuine prominent horses who may trade positions behind Clocker in the early furlongs; whichever secures the closer tracking berth on the inner is better placed to strike late.
Path To Peace — flagged as fading in finishes and has poor recent form; on soft ground over 1m5f with hold-up style, there is a real risk of tailing off and connections should be monitored pre-race.

Billy No Mates and Aighear — two veteran stayers with 75 and 48 days off respectively, both racing out of their natural hold-up roles; if either drifts markedly in the market, it may signal stable confidence is low heading in.

Spanish Hustle — Paul Mulrennan's booking stands out given his quality relative to horse's OR of 62 and modest recent form; watch the market for any unusual activity that might suggest connections expect improvement.

races.name: Molton Brown Luxury Fragrance Hamilton Park 2-y-o Series Final Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Battle Fever
runners_data.note: Consistent front-end performer rated OR 88, Kevin Stott partners a horse who has placed four times from four runs and handles soft ground (1 sim-going run, placed); looks the class horse in the field and is ideally positioned to press the pace and strike.

runners_data.name: Harley
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the ride for the in-form Edward Bethell yard; has won and placed repeatedly over this exact trip in good ground but steps onto soft for the first time — the ground is a minor question mark but the 6f trip suits and the prominent style is perfect for this race shape.

runners_data.name: Rbflying
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's gelding sports a tongue tie and has shown flickers of ability (third at 6f on good ground) but its recent form includes two poor efforts on soft and good-to-soft at 7f; by inclination a hold-up horse, it will not get the far back position it prefers with fellow hold-up types filling the rear — the style mismatch tempers its prospects meaningfully.

runners_data.name: Onslaught
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey have placed this youngster three times from four, all over five furlongs on good ground, so both the step up to six furlongs and the soft surface are unexplored territory; its natural hold-up tendency means it will be squeezed into a midfield slot rather than the rear where it does its best work, making the conditions doubly unfamiliar.

runners_data.name: Boutblummintime
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's filly — 33 days off the track, no wins and modest OR 61 — is the lone confirmed pace-setter and will shape the entire race by the tempo she sets; her soft-going record is 0W0P from one run and Finlay Bassett (7lb claim) must judge the pace carefully on a surface that can expose a weak finisher.

runners_data.name: Trumpety Trump
runners_data.note: Lauren Young (5lb) rides for Jim Goldie and this is the most credible of the hold-up contenders, having finished second over 8f on soft and third over 6f on good; the step back to 6f from her most recent start on soft is a potential concern but she carries genuine soft-ground form and is the truest late-runner in the field.

runners_data.name: Wild Terrain
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's gelding (blinkers and tongue tie) returns just six days after its last run and its form string of 10007 flags a worrying fade pattern — the analyst has flagged it as one that tends to stop in the finish; a single win to its name came on good ground and all its soft-surface runs have been poor.

runners_data.name: Sea Mirage
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's second string sits well in the prominent group and has placed twice over 5-6 furlongs including a runner-up finish on soft; Shay Farmer (5lb) is an economy booking and the horse's OR 71 means it is not without a chance if the race sets up for the placed horses just off the leader's back.

races.paceDynamic: Boutblummintime is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge, should dictate from the gates at a measured tempo on soft ground over six furlongs at Hamilton. Battle Fever, Harley, and Sea Mirage will press from the front group, creating a competitive but not suicidal early gallop that suits those who can travel prominently and sustain their effort. Rbflying and Onslaught are genuine hold-up types by inclination but the field holds more back-end horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — both are likely to end up racing closer to midfield than their natural style demands, meaning the true closing kick scenario is weakened. Soft ground at Hamilton rewards those who settle close to the pace and grind through the conditions rather than waiting for a late surge, so the prominent profile — horses who can sit just off the leader and pounce in the final furlong — is best positioned to capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Boutblummintime gets a clean break and sets a sustainable tempo, with prominently-placed rivals able to stalk and strike.
scenarios.body: Boutblummintime dictates an honest but manageable gallop on soft ground, and the horses sat just off the pace — Battle Fever and Harley — are able to engage in the final two furlongs and grind past; soft ground rewards the relentless traveller over the late sprinter.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If Boutblummintime goes off too fast for the conditions and ties up, leaving the door open for runners coming from deeper.
scenarios.body: The front runners empty in the final furlong on a testing surface and the horses who have been forced into midfield — Rbflying or Onslaught — manage to make ground despite racing out of their ideal role; however this scenario is discounted because neither is a true late closer in this race shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Boutblummintime sets a very modest tempo and the prominent horses fail to reel her in under soft conditions.
scenarios.body: A slow early pace on the soft surface paradoxically disadvantages those trying to close from midfield, and Boutblummintime — rated only OR 61 but well-placed on the front end — hangs on as rivals fail to find their best closing gears; Sea Mirage, close throughout, could grab a place.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Early Pace, Hold-Up Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent trio press hard from the off and the pace becomes genuinely strong, opening a late run from deep.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop burns off the front group and allows a hold-up horse to weave through late, but given Rbflying's and Onslaught's compromised positions this is the least likely shape to materialise; Trumpety Trump, the only genuine hold-up runner with soft-ground form, is the primary beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Battle Fever is the highest-rated runner (OR 88) with the most consistent recent form — if Kevin Stott can slot in just behind Boutblummintime from stall position, this horse is the primary threat throughout the final two furlongs.

Boutblummintime (Finlay Bassett, 7lb claim) sets the entire tempo from the front — watch the early fractions closely; if she goes off too hard on soft ground she risks weakening badly and dragging the race shape into chaos for those behind.

Rbflying and Onslaught are both genuine hold-up horses who will be unable to get to the rear of the field — monitor where they settle in the first furlong; if they are forced wide or into a contested midfield position their chance diminishes significantly.

Wild Terrain's six-day turnaround and repeated fade pattern in the finish on softer surfaces is worth noting — if it shows prominently early, it may be a false position and runners coming from behind it in the final furlong should benefit.

The entire race is being run on a soft surface with every card race today also soft — the going is consistent throughout the day, so no prospect of the ground drying and favouring firmer-ground types in a late-race surprise.

races.name: Follow Us On X @hamiltonparkrc Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Call Me Betty
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on soft last time out and has placed twice at 7f on standard-to-slow, giving her the strongest soft-ground profile in the field; hold-up style suits the expected shape but the 86-day absence is worth noting alongside Connor Beasley's booking.

runners_data.name: Mae Amor
runners_data.note: No soft-going form in her last five starts (all good), which is a meaningful concern today; David Allan retains the ride for Rebecca Menzies but the visor flag and lack of cut-ground evidence make this one to treat cautiously.

runners_data.name: Diamont Katie
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's operation has nine winners from 46 runners in the past 14 days indicating strong stable form; hold-up style suits a controlled pace, and her consistent placed record over 6-7f on good suggests she handles pace variation — soft is unexplored but trip is right.

runners_data.name: Pickersgill
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse placed over 6f on standard and 7f on standard for Iain Jardine; mapped to midfield due to redistribution, meaning she is likely racing ahead of her comfort zone — her 0W0P soft-going record further tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Kilfrush Desert
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's three-year-old has placed twice over 6f on standard (all weather) and shows good consistency; natural hold-up racer pushed into a midfield mapping because the rear is overcrowded, so she may not get the clean late run her style demands.

runners_data.name: Annie Edson Taylor
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good last time and wears a tongue-strap today; her hold-up style is her natural game but she's been placed into midfield on the map — the 1W3P record at 6f on similar going hints at competitiveness, though soft is one step beyond her proven range.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Kisses
runners_data.note: Ran only 12 days ago (finishing sixth on soft, her only soft-ground run) so recency is fine and she has a soft-ground reference; a three-year-old with 0W0P on soft, she holds natural hold-up tendencies but is mapped to midfield in a congested scenario.

runners_data.name: Lily Pearl
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the race and the single horse with a clean path to the lead; Richard and Fahey's filly won over 6f on soft which is the key credential, though 90 days off the track and a STYLE_FIT flag (she's a prominent type mapped to lead) means any rustiness could be exposed.

runners_data.name: Thunderstorm Katie
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good last time and has placed at 5-6f for Jim Goldie; a genuine hold-up type whose natural game is a late run, but the map has her in midfield because the rear is oversubscribed — Lauren Young takes the 5lb claim which gives a small compensation.

runners_data.name: Invincible Ruby
runners_data.note: Has won twice over 6f on good for Iain Jardine and Jardine's stable also runs Pickersgill today; a natural hold-up horse positioned in midfield due to redistribution, carrying a 0W0P soft-going record that adds another layer of uncertainty.

races.paceDynamic: Lily Pearl is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to push her, she should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on soft ground at Hamilton's six furlongs. The pace dynamic is therefore a single-setter scenario: Lily Pearl leads at her own tempo, which on soft going over six furlongs is likely to be honest rather than suicidal, meaning the race will not collapse in a heap at the front. Several horses in this field — Thunderstorm Katie, Kilfrush Desert, Invincible Ruby, and others — are natural hold-up or prominent types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field simply cannot accommodate every horse in its preferred position, so the mid-pack will be congested and the racing room picture is a genuine concern. With one uncontested leader setting a measured soft-ground tempo and a bunch of hold-up types forced to race closer than ideal, the tactical verdict is clear: horses with proven soft-ground form who can pick off a controlled leader from a true off-the-pace position, or who have the class to peg Lily Pearl back in the final furlong, hold the structural advantage — genuine hold-up runners with soft-going evidence are favoured, while those redistributed from the rear to midfield are structurally compromised.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lily Pearl Controls Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Lily Pearl secures the lead unchallenged and dictates a controlled soft-ground tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Lily Pearl has winning soft-ground form and, facing no pace rival, sets every fraction to suit herself; soft going rewards a horse that travels smoothly in front rather than one that has to battle for the early call.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Her In
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground slows the pace enough that a true hold-up horse arrives fresh and powerful in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A measured gallop on testing ground ultimately tests stamina in the closing stages, and a runner with genuine soft-going credentials storming from off the pace has the ground working in its favour; Call Me Betty's recent soft-ground win and Diamont Katie's consistent placed form make them the most credible closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a redistributed hold-up type such as Invincible Ruby or Thunderstorm Katie secures an unexpectedly prominent position and uses it to time a run perfectly.
scenarios.body: Should the midfield congestion resolve early and one of these horses travel into contention, the tactical scenario changes materially; however, both carry STYLE_FIT discounts because this position is not their natural home, reducing the probability this shape delivers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the ground is more testing than the soft description implies and the race becomes a thorough stamina test that exposes those without proven soft-going form.
scenarios.body: In a true slog, Lily Pearl's uncontested lead becomes a liability as she tires in the final furlong and only those with demonstrated soft-going resilience survive; Mae Amor's going concern flags make this scenario unlikely to suit her, while runners with genuine soft-ground placed form hold residual claims.

watchPoints.text: Lily Pearl's 90-day absence is the single biggest variable in this race — if she is short of peak fitness, the entire pace map unravels because she is the only horse capable of setting a sustainable lead.

Midfield congestion is a serious concern: Thunderstorm Katie, Kilfrush Desert, Invincible Ruby, Pickersgill, and Annie Edson Taylor are all natural hold-up types crowded into the same part of the track — watch for traffic problems and interference in the final two furlongs at Hamilton's tight finishing straight.

Mae Amor's visor flag (hg:v) suggests a trainer intervention to sharpen her up, but her complete absence of soft-going form means any ground-related deterioration could render the headgear irrelevant — monitor market moves.

Call Me Betty's 86-day layoff is notable, but her soft-ground win last time and Michael Dods' T14 strike rate (4/27) suggest the stable sends them fit — her going profile is the strongest match for today's conditions if she's ready to run.

Hamilton's six furlongs on soft can become a stamina test in the closing stages; horses drawn wide may face additional ground — check final draw positions for any that may need to travel further than rivals.

races.name: #cleanstay At Hampton By Hilton Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Tee Aitch Aye
runners_data.note: Soft-going record of 7/15 includes a win and four places, making him comfortably the most at home in today's conditions; Jack Nicholls (3lb) claim is a bonus, and the step back up to 12.5f suits a horse who stayed on well over 10f last time — a genuine soft-ground stayer to respect.

runners_data.name: Palmarian
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have been on good ground and at shorter trips of seven to eight furlongs, so today's soft conditions and 12.5f trip represent a significant double query; zero wins or places in soft going from two attempts is a flag that cannot be ignored.

runners_data.name: Keats House
runners_data.note: Has run five times on good or soft ground at eight to nine furlongs and shown modest but consistent mid-division efforts; Billy Garritty takes over and the step up in trip to 12.5f is untested, but the consistent finishing pattern suits a prominent racing style if the pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Kelpie Grey
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter in this field, which gives Paul Mulrennan complete control of the race tempo; however, all five recent starts have been at six to seven furlongs on soft or good, making this 12.5f trip a dramatic step up in distance that raises a genuine stamina question at the most important moment of the race.

runners_data.name: Penelope's Sister
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by profile — soft-going form of 8/15 includes a win and five places, and the 10f trip last time showed she stays well — but she is mapped to midfield because the field's rear is oversubscribed, meaning she may not get the clean run her style requires.

runners_data.name: Yaaser
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran for Jim Goldie who has placed three times in seven recent soft-ground starts, though usually at shorter trips of seven to eight furlongs; his true style is hold-up but the congested field forces him into midfield, and Lauren Young's 5lb claim does not fully offset the trip concern.

runners_data.name: Mimi's Magic
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope is a significant booking for Ed Dunlop's three-year-old, who has climbed to a peak of 9/8f/STA last time out after a promising 2/10f/STA run; the historical trip form over ten furlongs is encouraging but soft going is untested, and the weight allowance at 132lbs helps.

runners_data.name: Aurelune
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr takes the ride for the Fahey yard after a 60-day absence; two of five runs have been on soft or standard ground with a placed effort, and while the three-year-old has some mid-distance experience over 10f on soft, the layoff and the fact she is running away from her best position are both mild concerns.

runners_data.name: Scheffler
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners this three-year-old who has one soft-ground start from six career runs, finishing tenth; form figures of 399047 show limited reliability, and like several others in this race, the horse is filing into midfield despite a natural tendency to race from behind — the overall profile is hard to warm to.

runners_data.name: Toy Soldier
runners_data.note: Carries headgear and a stamina warning — the "fades in finish" flag is a meaningful concern on soft ground over 12.5f, the longest trip in the field; Lexie Clarkson's 7lb claim helps the weight but this horse has two placed efforts on soft without converting, and its true hold-up nature, squeezed into midfield, leaves it tactically disadvantaged.

races.paceDynamic: Kelpie Grey is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will bowl along at a sustainable clip on soft ground over this mile-and-a-half trip at Hamilton. That uncontested lead is likely to be a true lone-ranger scenario — soft going will keep sectionals honest rather than suicidal, meaning the pace will be measured rather than brutal. The vast majority of this field are natural hold-up or come-from-behind types, and with Penelope's Sister, Yaaser, Aurelune, Scheffler and Toy Soldier all redistributed from their natural rear positions into a congested midfield, the map is carrying more closers than it can cleanly accommodate. In this shape — a soft-ground lone leader controlling the tempo — horses who can race prominently in behind Kelpie Grey and travel into the race, rather than those forced wide or stuck in traffic from deep, are best positioned, making a well-placed prominent or flexible mid-division type who can attack from two furlongs out the most favoured profile. The field holds more hold-up types than can find their natural position; of those most likely to actually secure a handy berth, Keats House and Tee Aitch Aye are best placed to get closer to the pace than their rivals.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kelpie Grey Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Kelpie Grey is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a soft but unrelenting gallop that saps the closers on heavy ground.
scenarios.body: Kelpie Grey controls every fraction from the front, the soft surface extending the leader's advantage as hold-up horses struggle to close from a deep midfield pack; a prominent horse traveling sweetly in behind is best placed to pick up the scraps.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate and a horse sitting second or third travelling strongly swoops inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A horse like Tee Aitch Aye or Penelope's Sister, having stalked Kelpie Grey at close quarters, produces a sustained run on the soft ground once the leader ties up late; soft-ground course form and stamina are decisive at this distance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the midfield pack collectively gets a better trip than expected and the front end cracks in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Soft ground and an honest pace could see the leader pay late, opening a gap for a horse like Mimi's Magic or Aurelune to rattle home; however, with most true closers displaced from their natural positions, their ability to produce a genuine late burst is structurally compromised.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Shape
scenarios.trigger: If a slow start or scrimmaging in the congested midfield causes interference that reshuffles the whole race.
scenarios.body: With so many horses packed into mid-division and running out of their natural role, a rough passage or slow pace followed by a sprint could produce a shock result; Palmarian or Scheffler, finding a clear run late, could capitalise on a messy race.

watchPoints.text: Kelpie Grey's stamina is the race's pivotal question — if this confirmed front-runner fails to stay the 12.5f on soft ground, the entire predicted race shape collapses and hold-up types rushing home late become suddenly viable.

The Jim Goldie trio of Penelope's Sister, Yaaser and Kelpie Grey are all running today from the same yard; watch for any signs of team tactics or for one of the yard's closers to be given an instructive conditional ride behind their own front-runner.

With five or more true hold-up horses crammed into mid-division, a traffic jam in the straight is highly likely on soft ground — watch which of Aurelune, Scheffler, Toy Soldier or Mimi's Magic finds the clearest passage turning for home.

Palmarian's complete absence of soft-ground or stamina form is worth monitoring in the market — if supported despite those flags, it may signal a significant stable confidence that the horse has improved or handles cut ground in home work.

Tee Aitch Aye's soft-going profile (one win, four places from 15 starts) stands out as statistically the most reliable in today's conditions — watch whether Jack Nicholls elects to track the leader from the outset rather than dropping out in his usual hold-up role.

races.name: Book Your Christmas Party Hamilton Park Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Annandale
runners_data.note: Consistent soft-going performer for Jim Goldie who has placed in several 13f races on good ground; Paul Mulrennan is a strong booking, and the hold-up style suits a scenario where Falaise Blanc sets a retrievable pace — last ran just 6 days ago suggesting yard confidence.

runners_data.name: Sophiesticate
runners_data.note: Won over 13f on good recently and has placed form at 12f-15f; Shay Farmer claims 5lb which is a useful weight relief, and her hold-up style means she needs to find a clear run in what will be a congested rear section — soft-ground figures are modest (1W1P from 15 runs) so the going is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Dubai Venture
runners_data.note: Solid recent form including a soft-ground placing; in reality this horse prefers to race from the back but the field's hold-up bias means it has been assigned to midfield on the map — the 5lb penalty for a recent win is the key handicap factor, and soft-going form is limited (0W1P).

runners_data.name: Vampire Slayer
runners_data.note: Strong soft-ground record (2W5P from 12 runs in similar conditions) is the headline here, having won twice at 16f-17f on soft; a 166-day absence is the one concern, but the headgear (p) note and those soft-ground wins make this horse interesting if it returns fit — genuinely holds up and will need clean passage.

runners_data.name: Hickton
runners_data.note: Won over 14f on standard going recently but the majority of placed form is on all-weather or standard surfaces; this is a natural hold-up horse whose best chance depends on getting a clear run in a congested field — soft-going form is limited and the 13d turnaround means the Declan Carroll yard is clearly keen.

runners_data.name: Uncle Liam
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on good ground for Jim Goldie but all soft-going runs have been well beaten; Daniel Tudhope is an excellent booking for the stable and the horse drops back to a workable OR of 52, but the 59-day break and preference for faster ground make conditions a genuine question — needs the pace to be genuinely slow.

runners_data.name: Falaise Blanc
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in this field and will lead from the front unchallenged; headgear (v) noted, and while soft-going form figures (0W2P) are unspectacular, dictating an uncontested lead in soft conditions represents a completely different proposition to being ridden to the pace by others — the Katie Scott yard has a poor recent strike rate (0/10 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Dandy's Angel
runners_data.note: Oldest runner in the field at 9 and recent form figures are uninspiring including a couple of poor efforts on soft; Connor Beasley is a capable jockey but this horse has been running short at 8f-10f lately and faces a significant step up in trip — held up by nature but gets squeezed into midfield by the field's composition.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Nature
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's third runner on the card and typically races from off the pace; a young 4-year-old with soft-going form limited to two efforts (0W0P), the horse has been well beaten in recent starts and Lauren Young's 5lb claim is the main positive — trip looks fine but the overall profile suggests this is a difficult race to win.

races.paceDynamic: Falaise Blanc is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rivals willing or able to push forward aggressively, will dictate a controlled, measured gallop on soft ground at Hamilton over 1m3f — a genuine case of one horse owning the pace. The absence of any true second pace-setter means Falaise Blanc can dictate on her own terms, and in soft conditions that self-made tempo is likely to be modest rather than searching, creating a race that will be run at an even keel before the tempo rises in the final two furlongs. The field behind is saturated with hold-up types — Dubai Venture, Hickton, Uncle Liam, Dandy's Angel, and Spirit Of Nature are all natural rear-rangers who have been redistributed into midfield on the pace map simply because there is nowhere else to put them, meaning the actual rear will be extremely congested and the race may develop into a grinding cavalry charge off a slow pace. This shape strongly favours a horse that can travel prominently behind the leader or arrive with one smooth run from just off the pace, since closers will find themselves bunched together and reliant on the soft ground to level the playing field — prominent-tracking profiles are best placed here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Falaise Blanc Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Falaise Blanc leads from the front unopposed and sets a moderate soft-ground tempo that softens the closers' finishing kicks.
scenarios.body: Falaise Blanc bowls along at a controlled gallop with Rowan Scott dictating every yard, and the congested hold-up pack spends the whole race manoeuvring for position rather than building momentum; the winner emerges from within striking range of the leader rather than from the back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travelling just behind Falaise Blanc travels smoothly and picks up powerfully in the straight as the pace-setter ties up.
scenarios.body: Annandale or Sophiesticate, both suited by soft ground and this distance bracket, tracks the modest tempo and produces a well-timed challenge inside the final furlong; the slow early fractions mean they have not been asked a question until the decisive moment.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Storms Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow enough to compress the field and a genuine closer threads through on soft ground in the final stages.
scenarios.body: Vampire Slayer, who has strong soft-ground form and has been running at longer trips, or Dubai Venture, who has proven soft-ground ability, benefits if the bunched hold-up group finds a clear run; however, given that most closers here are redistibuted types rather than genuine hold-up horses, this scenario carries real execution risk.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Fails To Quicken
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground deteriorates the gallop to a crawl and multiple horses struggle to pick up, resulting in a messy outcome with a low-rated improver stealing it.
scenarios.body: A chaotic finish where Hickton or Uncle Liam, neither a natural hold-up horse despite the mapping, finds an unexpected gap as the field idles; this is the least likely shape given the clear pace dynamic but soft ground always carries an element of unpredictability with a large hold-up dominated field.

watchPoints.text: Falaise Blanc's front-running tactics are unchallenged — if Rowan Scott jumps cleanly and establishes the lead within the first furlong, watch how long it takes for any rival to apply pressure; if none do, the race could be effectively decided by halfway on this soft ground.

The hold-up section is dangerously congested — Dubai Venture, Hickton, Uncle Liam, Dandy's Angel and Spirit Of Nature are all natural rear-rangers crammed into a small patch of ground, and a traffic incident or bunching in the straight is a realistic risk that could compromise multiple fancied runners.

Vampire Slayer has not run for 166 days — watch in the paddock and at the start for signs of freshness; the soft-ground form is excellent when fit but a long absence on a soft Hamilton track is a combination that needs validating in the pre-race build-up.

Jim Goldie runs three horses (Annandale, Uncle Liam, Spirit Of Nature) — watch for any stable market moves and note whether Daniel Tudhope on Uncle Liam or Paul Mulrennan on Annandale attracts the stronger support, as that could signal which the yard most fancies.
